A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same inference-time reinforcement-learning study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite added sections and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations across 17 multi-agent tasks, including comparisons of inference strategies, compute-scaling results and measured solution counts.

after.justification: V2 retains the original multi-agent experiments and adds an original single-agent Craftax evaluation in Appendix C.1.

M1.justification: The four inference strategies, their multi-agent adaptations, COMPASS training and Algorithms 1–4 are unchanged. Expanded explanations and parameter-count disclosures do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds one single-agent Craftax-1B evaluation while retaining all 17 Connector, RWARE and SMACv2 tasks. The other single-agent problems discussed in Appendix C.2 concern published literature, not additional experiments by this work.

E2.justification: Figure 8 adds SABLE+SGBS to the smacv2_10_units comparison, whose results v1 explicitly withheld because of an issue. The remaining comparator membership and the underlying method families are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds the Craftax comparison of zero-shot SABLE with 30-second stochastic sampling. It also revises the reported SGBS settings: v1 Table 4 specifies beam width 4, whereas v2 Table 5 specifies expansion factor 4 and beam widths from 1 to 64. This changes the stated settings without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds a quantitative analysis of COMPASS's model-size overhead relative to each base policy, supported by Tables 8–10. No new controlled component ablations or robustness tests are reported; Appendix K mainly adds explanatory discussion.

E5.justification: Appendix L newly supplies per-task 95% bootstrap intervals for the existing Figure 4 comparison through Table 17 and Figure 12. It also specifies 10 runs for the inherited 20M-step baseline. The 128-run reporting for the work's evaluations was already present; an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports Craftax mean scores of 18.8% for zero-shot inference and 25.8% for 30-second sampling, approximately a 37% relative gain within this new experiment. Figure 8 supplies the previously missing SABLE+SGBS results. Figures 1–7 and the retained solution-count tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: The Dec-POMDP definition, training objective and budget-constrained inference formulation are retained. V2 adds no substantive formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions and headline claims remain unchanged: inference strategies overcome zero-shot ceilings, with 45% average and 126% maximum improvement across 17 tasks and favorable SABLE+COMPASS scaling. Craftax supports the previously stated expectation of single-agent applicability.

C2.justification: The limitations discussion replaces an entirely untested single-agent extension with explicitly limited Craftax evidence. Appendices H and K add practical applicability explanations and further arguments about COMPASS's multiple-attempt objective, policy diversity and low-dimensional search relative to full-policy fine-tuning.

D1.justification: Appendix I newly discloses base-policy and COMPASS parameter counts and relative increases. V2 also updates the code/data landing-page address and removes the forthcoming-repository footnote. Existing training budgets, implementation-stack descriptions and COMPASS initialization details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused discussion connecting and distinguishing inference strategies from meta-RL and offline-to-online RL, with references including VariBAD, RL2, MAML, DIMES and Cal-QL. Craftax is also newly cited. Bello and MEMENTO publication updates correspond to already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 removes 'Complex' from the title, makes local wording and paragraph changes, expands explanatory passages and adds appendix sections. The existing main narrative, method descriptions and experimental exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Craftax and parameter-count tables, completes Figure 8, and redisplays the Figure 4 comparison with confidence intervals in Figure 12 and Table 17. Existing displays are resized, relocated or renumbered within the same overall visual format.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves empirical breadth and transparency: Craftax provides initial evidence for a previously untested extension, Figure 8 completes a withheld comparison, and Appendices I and L clarify model sizes and uncertainty. These gains leave the core study intact. Some new precision issues remain, notably Appendix I's 'below 1.6%' statement despite Tables 8–9 reaching 1.65%, but they do not outweigh the improvements.
